definitions.explanation: A person's official title, rank, or position, especially as used on business cards or in formal introductions.

examples.japanese: {名刺|めいし}に{肩書|かたがき}を{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Put your title on your business card.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{肩書|かたがき}は{部長|ぶちょう}だ。
{肩書|かたがき}だけで{人|ひと}を{判断|はんだん}してはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't judge people only by their titles.

notes:
FORMS:
{肩|かた} (shoulder) + {書|がき} (writing) — originally referred to text written above a person's name, where titles were placed.

WRITING:
Also written as {肩書|かたがき}き with okurigana.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肩書|かたがき}がある: to have a title
- {肩書|かたがき}にこだわる: to be particular about titles
- {立派|りっぱ}な{肩書|かたがき}: an impressive title

USAGE:
In Japanese business culture, {肩書|かたがき} is important for establishing hierarchy and proper etiquette. Business cards ({名刺|めいし}) always include one's title.
